final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest applicable EVEscape score (z=0.781) with strong PLM plausibility (0.984). Glycine-to-aspartate in a GP1 epitope surface loop is a classic charge-altering antibody escape mechanism while preserving the overall fold.
Applicable EVEscape z=0.674 and perfect PLM plausibility; H115 lies near the 12.1F epitope and H->N is a natural, well-tolerated substitution that can perturb antibody contact.
Direct applicable phenotype evidence (EVEscape z=0.562) supports escape benefit, but low PLM plausibility (0.290) tempers confidence in functional preservation and keeps it at rank 3.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 is stable with direct applicable phenotype evidence for each candidate and no tool call left that could materially change the ranking.

history.rationale: GP1 surface residue in the antibody-accessible head region; H→N removes a charged epitope contact while conserving size, plausibly reducing 12.1F/37.2D binding. Not part of the entry-critical FVR triad.
Position 115 lies in the GP1 receptor-binding region; H→N is a conservative glycosylation-compatible change near the 12.1F footprint. No phenotype evidence available, so prior stands.
Strong EVEscape score (0.674) with excellent PLM plausibility (1.0). H115 lies in the 8.9F epitope region; conservative H->N change likely preserves folding.
Solid EVEscape z (0.674, applicable) and maximal PLM plausibility (1.000). Loss of a His at an antibody-contact position plausibly disrupts 12.1F-class contacts.

Applicable EVEscape z=0.674 with perfect PLM score; H115 sits near the 12.1F epitope and H->N removes a glycosylation-adjacent histidine while remaining a plausible natural substitution. Retain at rank 2.
Charge-reversal at a GP1 residue near antigenic loop reported to contribute to 8.9F/37.2D epitopes; alters antibody contact without touching receptor-binding residues H141/F147/Y150.

Charge-reversal at a surface-exposed GP1 position is a plausible epitope-disrupting move, but the phenotype tool returned no usable evidence. Slight confidence reduction pending structural/PLM checks.

Charge-reversal at a solvent-exposed GP1 position is mechanistically plausible for antibody escape and PLM-neutral, but no EVEscape score is available. Retained pending structural/viability evidence next round.
High PLM plausibility but both phenotype calls returned inapplicable (app=0.00), so no direct escape support; demoted below N119D.
Both EVEscape calls returned inapplicable (z=?, app=0) and confidence has decayed from 0.35 to 0.10 across rounds. Dropping to leave a clean Top-3 with direct phenotype support.

rejection.reason: Both EVEscape calls returned inapplicable (z=?, app=0) and confidence has decayed from 0.35 to 0.10 across rounds. Dropping to leave a clean Top-3 with direct phenotype support.

history.rationale: Loop position adjacent to the GP1 antigenic surface; insertion of negative charge may disrupt antibody binding and is distant from known entry-critical sites.
Glycine-to-acidic substitution on a GP1 loop can alter antibody contact geometry; retained as a moderately risky epitope-targeted candidate.
Highest EVEscape score (0.781) among all candidates with good PLM plausibility (0.984). Promoted to rank 1; G160 sits on the GP1 surface near antibody contact residues.

Highest EVEscape z (0.781, applicable) with strong PLM plausibility (0.984); charge addition at an epitope-facing GP1 position supports escape. Structure evidence unavailable (no coordinates), so no structural penalty applies.

Highest applicable EVEscape score (z=0.781) and strong PLM plausibility; glycine-to-aspartate at an epitope surface loop is a classic charge-reversal escape mechanism. Structural tool was inapplicable (no coordinates), which does not contradict the design.
Surface-exposed GP1 position; charge addition can weaken neutralizing antibody interaction while leaving the LAMP1-binding region and SSP/entry machinery intact.
Retained pending structure/PLM evidence; phenotype call was uninformative.
PLM-neutral but no phenotype score and uncertain epitope relevance. Kept as backup only.
PLM plausibility is not a phenotype signal; both EVEscape calls inapplicable and epitope relevance is weak.

rejection.reason: PLM plausibility is not a phenotype signal; both EVEscape calls inapplicable and epitope relevance is weak.

history.rationale: Position in GP1 distal domain; conservative hydrophobic substitution with potential to alter local epitope topology for 12.1F without gross folding disruption.
Retained pending alternate evidence sources; phenotype call uninformative.
No escape evidence and lowest PLM plausibility (0.53). Demoted to last; candidate for rejection next round.
No applicable phenotype evidence, lowest PLM score in the pool, and hydrophobic substitution in SSIM/GP2-adjacent region risks entry function.

rejection.reason: No applicable phenotype evidence, lowest PLM score in the pool, and hydrophobic substitution in SSIM/GP2-adjacent region risks entry function.

history.rationale: Near GP1 C-terminus/GP2 interface but outside the conserved fusion peptide; conservative aromatic substitution may modify antibody footprint while preserving entry.
Retained pending alternate evidence sources; phenotype call uninformative.
Conservative aromatic substitution with good PLM score but no phenotype evidence; weak epitope relevance keeps it low-ranked.
Conservative aromatic substitution with no applicable phenotype evidence and no structural support; escape benefit unlikely.

rejection.reason: Conservative aromatic substitution with no applicable phenotype evidence and no structural support; escape benefit unlikely.

history.rationale: Glycosylation-adjacent residue; mutation may alter glycan-independent antibody contacts; modest risk of folding effects to be checked by structure/PLM tools.
Retained; surface GP1 position with modest epitope-disruption potential.
EVEscape 0.562 supports escape, but the ESM-1v score (0.29) suggests low mutation plausibility, risking fitness/entry. Demoted below K124E.
Applicable EVEscape z=0.562 beats candidates with no usable phenotype evidence; promoted to rank 3. Low PLM score (0.290) is a viability caution but does not outweigh direct escape evidence.

Applicable EVEscape z=0.562 supports escape benefit, though PLM plausibility is low (0.290), so confidence is tempered. Retain as rank 3 since it is the only other candidate with direct applicable phenotype evidence.
Loop-constraint mutation in antigenic region could reshape epitope geometry; viability risk moderate, to be evaluated with structure compatibility.
Proline in a GP1 loop risks local backbone disruption affecting folding/entry; no supporting evidence obtained.

rejection.reason: Proline in a GP1 loop risks local backbone disruption affecting folding/entry; no supporting evidence obtained.

history.rationale: Conservative substitution in GP1 near the entry machinery region; low escape probability but low viability risk, retained as a safe fallback candidate.
Conservative hydrophobic substitution is unlikely to alter antibody binding; weak epitope relevance.

rejection.reason: Conservative hydrophobic substitution is unlikely to alter antibody binding; weak epitope relevance.

history.rationale: Backbone-disrupting mutation that could substantially alter local epitope structure; high risk to GP1 fold, kept for evidence-based reevaluation or rejection.
Proline likely destabilizes the GP1 core and could impair folding/entry without clear escape benefit.

rejection.reason: Proline likely destabilizes the GP1 core and could impair folding/entry without clear escape benefit.
